title: Close locally created resources
why: A locally owned file, socket, client, cursor, or database session can leak operating-system or connection-pool resources when no close boundary is visible.
suggestion: Use a context manager, close the resource in finally, or make the ownership transfer explicit by returning or storing it.
limitations: Only direct local assignments from common file, socket, HTTP client, cursor, and recognized requests or SQL session constructors are tracked.
Close calls, context-manager use, returns, yields, collection or attribute ownership transfers, chained constructor calls, and owner connection cleanup are accepted.
Cleanup or ownership transfer hidden behind arbitrary helper calls is not inferred, so this rule is advisory by default.
